title: Define the runtime identity, secret-reference, and V1 compatibility seam
body:
## Why / user outcome
Establish one stable runtime library seam for secret reads and identity/reference resolution. Preserve existing CLI behavior while making canonical identity independent of mutable names, paths, or provider-native IDs. Reading a secret must not grant write, replication, export, escrow, or signing authority.

## Current repository evidence
At source commit `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`, `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs` implements a name-only resolver with redacted `SecretValue`, source order, and broker/BWS fallback; `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/secrets.rs` implements only `get` and `list`. There is no typed canonical identity or scope/API. `fleet secrets get` intentionally prints the requested value to stdout; this is a caller-facing contract, not diagnostic logging. `cargo test --locked -p fleet-secrets` passed 16 tests on 2026-11-12, invoked bare with no resource wrapper or durable log.

## Scope and affected surface
Define additive public types and focused API tests in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/**`, with only the minimum `fleet` adapter needed. TRACE-02 owns the V1 CLI/profile golden corpus; this proposal consumes that legacy oracle and does not duplicate fixture/test ownership. Do not implement provider adapters, credential serialization/reconciliation, cache daemon changes, writer/admin APIs, PKI, generation, production reads, or a new crate. Coordinate the canonical credential schema with SEC-02; this seam defines identity/reference behavior, not its full record schema. A typed `RootPrivate` rejection does not protect V1 broker refresh or name-only BWS fallback: ROOT-09/OPS-10 must prove the legacy paths cannot access escrow scope before any copy. Trusted scope/native-ID exclusion or a separately least-privileged provider grant is required; a caller-supplied class or mutable sidecar is not sufficient. Affected files: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs`, `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/secrets.rs`, and focused tests under those crates; no provider config or data migration.

## API and behavior contract
Proposed typed shape:
```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
pub struct CredentialId(pub uuid::Uuid); // opaque canonical identity
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
pub struct SecretAlias { pub scope: ScopeId, pub name: String } // mutable locator
pub async fn resolve_alias(alias: &SecretAlias, cancel: CancellationToken)
    -> Result<CredentialId, AliasError>;
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
pub struct SecretRef { pub id: CredentialId, pub field: Option<FieldId> }
pub struct ResolutionContext {
    pub purpose: Purpose,
    pub offline_intent: OfflineIntent,
    pub required_assurance: AssuranceRequirement,
    pub caller_max_age: Option<Duration>, // only tightens stored policy
}
/// Private fields, loaded by the trusted server policy source, not supplied per request.
pub struct RevocationPolicy { /* opaque, server-owned policy */ }
pub struct AuthoritativeCredentialPolicy { /* private fields: stored class, revocation policy,
    verified provider/account/project/vault/native-ID binding, max age, offline permission,
    assurance floor */ }
#[async_trait]
pub trait AuthoritativePolicySource: Send + Sync {
    async fn load(&self, id: CredentialId, cancel: CancellationToken)
        -> Result<AuthoritativeCredentialPolicy, PolicyError>;
}
pub enum RevocationState { CurrentNotRevoked, Revoked, Unknown }
pub enum FreshnessDecision { Fresh, Degraded { reason: DegradedReason } }
pub enum DegradedReason { PolicyAuthorizedOfflineReplica, BoundedStaleUse }
pub struct ResolvedSecret {
    pub value: SecretBytes, // redacted Debug; no Clone/Serialize/Display
    pub source: ProviderId,
    pub native_revision: Option<Revision>,
    pub fetched_at: SystemTime,
    pub source_age: Duration,
    pub revocation: RevocationState,
    pub freshness: FreshnessDecision,
}
#[async_trait]
pub trait SecretStore: Send + Sync {
    async fn get(&self, id: CredentialId, field: Option<&FieldId>,
                 cancel: CancellationToken) -> Result<ProviderValue, ProviderError>;
}
pub struct Resolver { /* trusted policy source + injected stores/cache; no writer/signer */ }
impl Resolver {
    pub async fn resolve(&self, r: &SecretRef, context: &ResolutionContext,
                         cancel: CancellationToken) -> Result<ResolvedSecret, ResolveError>;
}
```
The per-call context contains purpose/offline intent/required assurance and optional max-age tightening, never stored class or revocation authority. Stored class/policy and scope/native binding come from the resolver's trusted policy source. Caller constraints can only tighten; self-labels or mutable sidecars cannot lower class. RootPrivate and RootSigning are denied by the ordinary resolver. Result includes source age and explicit fresh/degraded decision; any degraded success includes a typed reason. Revoked, policy-denied or insufficient-assurance values fail closed. PERF-02 owns freshness/revocation semantics; this packet defines the shared shape, not a second resolver or semantic owner.
## Measurable acceptance
1. A deterministic in-memory fake resolves by `CredentialId` without process spawn, filesystem or network.
2. Alias rename and provider/path relocation preserve `CredentialId`; same display name under different scopes never aliases.
3. Context exposes purpose/offline intent/required assurance and optional caller max age; trusted policy returns authoritative class/revocation/scope-binding and the caller cannot weaken it.
4. A fake-clock matrix varies stored class, purpose, online/offline request, assurance, revocation state and age for one logical ID. Oracle outcomes are fresh allow, bounded policy-authorized degraded use with explicit reason/source age, or denial. Revoked/high-risk deny overrides cache; no stale auto-fallback.
5. Ordinary typed resolver denies RootPrivate and its cache/prefetch/equality-index path. Legacy broker/BWS root exclusion is a separate ROOT-09/OPS-10 rollout gate and must be proved before any escrow copy.
6. API remains compatible with legacy CLI; TRACE-02 owns V1 golden stdout/stderr/exit fixtures and fixture/test work.
## Negative tests and oracle
Negative: alias collision, scope mismatch, path/name-derived ID, empty value, malformed provider response, caller attempt to downgrade authoritative class/assurance/revocation or self-assert RootPrivate/offline permission, revoked or unknown status under a must-check policy, and stale automatic fallback all fail closed. Oracle: fake provider plus authoritative policy registry and fake clock, reference policy-combination model, compile-time trait assertions (no `Serialize`/`Clone` on secret values), and output sentinel scan. CLI byte/exit oracles belong only to TRACE-02.

## Security and environment
Synthetic values only. No live provider access. Diagnostic output never contains value/token. Explicit stdout result remains permitted only as the legacy caller contract; callers needing stronger output control require a separate output policy.

## Dependencies, size, priority, lifecycle
Parent #9157; depends on #9156 TRACE-02 for the V1 compatibility oracle; SEC-02 consumes the opaque ID seam. Complexity M; V2; proposed High / urgency 450; Backlog.

## Rollback and recovery
Additive types can be removed while retaining legacy resolver and `get/list`. No persistent schema or external state changes. If typed API parity fails, keep old chain as default and disable the new API path; use TRACE-02’s V1 corpus as the CLI rollback oracle.

## Open decisions
Pick UUID representation/alias registry location only with SEC-02; do not store canonical identity in provider name/path or add a dependency/crate solely for an alias map.

## Priority semantics
The numeric `urgency` field is the shared charter intrinsic scale (lower is sooner); this score is High, distinct from importance, blocker, stage and dispatch. It is not the Project/queue priority. Do not change PM schema; any publisher maps High to queue priority 20 while retaining this numeric score and band in metadata/body.

title: Specify generic signer-session and artifact-sink authority interfaces
source_ranges: architecture-review.md ADR-S01, ADR-S04 and review/architecture-challenge.md A-2
stage: V2 shared contract; domain implementations later
body:
## Why / user outcome
Define only the shared authority interfaces for signer use and artifact output. An ordinary secret reference, inventory result, escrow read, or possession of key bytes must never confer signing authority. PKI graph construction and all algorithm/client implementation remain owned by #9163/#9164/#9162; general file transactions remain #9165.

## Current repository evidence
At `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`, Fleet has no signer, artifact-authority, or PKI module. `pkgs/id` Iroh endpoint identity is a separate identity type, not a root CA authorization contract. Parent ADR-S01 and the architecture challenge A-2 require transaction binding and anti-replay. ROOT-05 and CERT-03 already own PKI-specific implementation of that contract; this proposal owns only shared interface shape.

## Scope and technical boundaries
Specify typed signer authorization, session consumption, signer result/receipt and artifact sink authorization. Do not implement CA/issuer/leaf graph, algorithm registry/backends, PKI profiles, provider escrow, publication, output file transaction, or new CLI. The cohesive shared crypto contract may live in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-crypto/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs,tests/authorization.rs}` only if measured dependency closure makes it reusable by both generation and PKI; wire it opt-in in `pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml` and `pkgs/fleet/default.nix`. Do not create separate crates for authorization, signer, or artifact nouns. Affected files, if dependency closure justifies code: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-crypto/Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, `tests/authorization.rs`, and optional wiring in `pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml`/`pkgs/fleet/default.nix`; otherwise this is a documentation-only contract in this design packet.

## Proposed interface
The exact signing payload is prepared before authorization. Authority-bearing values have private constructors and no implicit `Clone`.
```rust
pub struct SigningAuthorization { // private fields; minted only by authority service
    root_key: AuthorizedKeyIdentity, // fingerprint/handle
    subject_spki: PublicKeyIdentity,
    signature_algorithm: SignatureAlgorithm,
    serial: Option<SerialNumber>,
    signed_payload_digest: Digest, // exact final TBS/message bytes
    profile: ProfileId,
    purpose: KeyPurpose,
    validity: ExactValidity,
    artifact_plan_digest: Digest,
    destinations: Vec<AuthorizedDestination>,
    expires_at: SystemTime,
    transaction_id: TransactionId,
    nonce: SingleUseNonce,
}
pub struct PreparedSigningTuple { /* private: SPKI, serial, exact TBS and plan digests */ }
pub struct PreparedIssuance { /* immutable final TBS + artifacts; private fields */ }
pub struct SignerSession { /* private, one validated authorization tuple */ }
pub struct DurableTupleClaim { /* private, atomic single-winner, non-Clone */ }
pub struct OutputAuthorization { /* private, exact plan/class/destination/expiry, non-Clone */ }
#[async_trait]
pub trait SigningAuthorizationPort: Send + Sync {
    async fn authorize_prepared(&self, tuple: &PreparedSigningTuple,
                                cancel: CancellationToken)
        -> Result<SignerSession, AuthorizationError>;
}
#[async_trait]
pub trait DurableAuthorizationLedger: Send + Sync {
    async fn consume_once(&self, session: &mut SignerSession, tuple_digest: Digest,
                          cancel: CancellationToken) -> Result<DurableTupleClaim, ClaimError>;
    async fn record_result(&self, claim: DurableTupleClaim,
                           result: SigningReceiptOrUncertain) -> Result<(), LedgerError>;
}
#[async_trait]
pub trait Signer: Send + Sync {
    async fn sign(&self, claim: &DurableTupleClaim, exact_tbs: &[u8],
                  cancel: CancellationToken) -> Result<SignatureReceipt, SignError>;
}
#[async_trait]
pub trait OutputAuthorizationPort: Send + Sync {
    async fn authorize_output(&self, plan: &ArtifactPlan, artifact: &ClassifiedArtifact,
                              cancel: CancellationToken)
        -> Result<OutputAuthorization, OutputAuthorizationError>;
}
#[async_trait]
pub trait ArtifactSink: Send {
    async fn write(&mut self, authorization: &OutputAuthorization,
                   artifact: ClassifiedArtifact, cancel: CancellationToken)
        -> Result<ArtifactReceipt, SinkError>;
}
pub struct PkiEngine { /* PKI profiles/graph; no embedded signer authority */ }
impl PkiEngine {
    pub async fn prepare_leaf(&self, req: LeafRequest, serials: &dyn SerialLedger,
                              clock: &dyn Clock, cancel: CancellationToken)
        -> Result<PreparedIssuance, PkiError>;
    pub async fn sign_prepared(&self, prepared: PreparedIssuance,
                               session: &mut SignerSession, claim: DurableTupleClaim,
                               signer: &dyn Signer, cancel: CancellationToken)
        -> Result<SignedIssuance, PkiError>;
    pub async fn issue_leaf(&self, req: LeafRequest,
                            authorization: &dyn SigningAuthorizationPort,
                            serials: &dyn SerialLedger, ledger: &dyn DurableAuthorizationLedger,
                            signer: &dyn Signer, clock: &dyn Clock, cancel: CancellationToken)
        -> Result<IssuedCertificate, PkiError>;
    pub async fn issue_root(&self, req: RootRequest, root_key: ExplicitRootKeyRef,
                            ceremony: &RootKeyCreationAuthorization,
                            authorization: &dyn SigningAuthorizationPort,
                            signer: &dyn Signer, ledger: &dyn DurableAuthorizationLedger,
                            cancel: CancellationToken) -> Result<RootArtifact, PkiError>;
}
```
The `issue_leaf` convenience helper prepares/reserves first and requests authorization only after SPKI, serial, exact TBS and artifact-plan digest are known; it never accepts a prefilled grant for unknown bytes. A dry run may show estimates/placeholders but cannot reserve a serial or mint final-TBS authorization. Root signing always names an explicit root key and separate key-creation/storage ceremony approval. A grant is single-tuple by default; multi-use must enumerate every final tuple. The ledger atomically consumes once before invoking the signer. Output authorization is separately minted for the exact plan/class/destination and cannot be derived from a signer grant.
## Measurable acceptance
1. An exact tuple grant binds root fingerprint/handle, subject SPKI, algorithm, serial, exact TBS digest, profile/purpose, validity, plan digest, destinations, expiry and transaction ID; mismatch is rejected before signing.
2. Two concurrent consumers race for one tuple; exactly one durable claim succeeds and signer invocation count is at most one.
3. Crash injection before claim, after claim/before signer call, after call/before receipt, and after receipt proves no duplicate invocation. A lost result with no authoritative status remains uncertain and blocked.
4. The high-level leaf helper only asks the authorization port after preparing final SPKI/serial/TBS/plan. Root helper requires an explicit key reference and separate ceremony approval; neither accepts a generic default signer.
5. Compile-fail/API tests show no signing without validated session/claim and no classified/private artifact write without `OutputAuthorization`; wrong destination, plan, class, expiry, or replay yields zero signer/sink calls.
6. ROOT-03/ROOT-04 synthetic signing uses this seam; their proposal dependencies include ARCH-06 and ROOT-05, or their bodies specify the same enforcement and tests. Direct signer bypass fails review/tests.
7. The interface stays in-memory and async; no private key bytes enter authority objects or receipts.
## Negative tests and oracle
Reject ambient/default signer discovery, signer substitution/fingerprint mismatch, changed plan digest, subject SPKI or algorithm mismatch, wrong purpose/profile, altered validity, unauthorized output/escrow destination, expired grant, replay, signer handle passed as `SecretRef`, or public-only grant used for private output. Oracle: model-based durable tuple state machine, synchronized two-consumer race, crash/fault injection, exact authorization/TBS digest comparison, fake invocation counters, authoritative-status fake, compile-fail/API fixtures showing no sign without claim and no private write without output grant, and redacted receipt golden fixture.

## Security and environment
Synthetic authorization and fake keys only. No production signing, key export, custody, DNS, trust-store or provider action.

## Dependencies, size, priority, lifecycle
Parent #9157; consumes plan/receipt schema OPS-01. Complexity M; V2 shared contract; proposed High / urgency 500; Backlog. ROOT-05 and CERT-03 implement PKI-specific adapters; GEN-04 consumes only after independent review.

## Rollback and recovery
Interface is additive and authority-denying by default. Disable fake adapter/feature if the model fails; do not relax mismatch checks to retain compatibility. No persistent state or production key changes.

## Open decisions
Concrete authorization token format, external approval ceremony and HSM attestation remain domain implementation decisions. The binding fields, durable atomic consume point, uncertain-status behavior, and refusal conditions are fixed; do not duplicate or weaken them in ROOT-05/CERT-03. ROOT-03/ROOT-04 synthetic graph fixtures must use this same authorized seam rather than direct signing.

## Priority semantics
The numeric `urgency` field is the shared charter intrinsic scale (lower is sooner); this score is High, distinct from importance, blocker, stage and dispatch. It is not the Project/queue priority. Do not change PM schema; any publisher maps High to queue priority 20 while retaining this numeric score and band in metadata/body.

title: Wire added domains through the existing Fleet registry and feature graph
source_ranges: fleet/crates/fleet-registry/src/lib.rs and fleet/crates/fleet/Cargo.toml at pinned census
stage: V2 registry contract; domain enablement by owners
body:
## Why / user outcome
Keep Fleet as the sole multicall CLI and make compiled, invocation-profile, and effective capabilities accurate as secrets/generation/PKI domains arrive. No competing CLI, CA server, or duplicate command registry.

## Current repository evidence
At `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`, `fleet-registry` is std-only and separates compiled/profile/effective capability sets. Existing domains have `secrets` but no `cert`/`pki` or `generate`. `fleet` Cargo features build full/serve/connect; `fleet-connect` is proxy-only with a stripped artifact hard cap of 2 MiB and target 1.5 MiB (`pkgs/fleet/default.nix`). Existing `get/list` output/exit contract is in `fleet/src/secrets.rs`.

## Scope and affected surface
Own registry descriptors, feature dependency wiring and capability tests in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-registry/**`, `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/Cargo.toml`, `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/**`, `pkgs/fleet/default.nix`, and registry/profile smoke tests under `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/tests/**`. Domain owners own command implementation. Add names/help stubs and feature declarations only when matching domain interface proposal exists. Keep existing aliases and CLI single-sourcing; optional `pki` alias may normalize to `cert`. No provider, PKI, reconciliation, docs generator or command functionality is implemented here.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A committed matrix enumerates compiled, invocation-profile and effective capability for full, serve, connect, consumer-min, agent and admin profiles.
2. Missing capability uses the existing registry unavailable behavior; help remains discoverable and accurately states prerequisites.
3. `fleet secrets get/list` stdout, stderr, exit semantics and broker/BWS order remain compatible. Secret stdout remains intentional and only diagnostics are redacted.
4. Command descriptors resolve from one registry source; help, JSON capability output, completion and dispatch agree.
5. No new profile name widens compiled capabilities; configuration cannot enable an uncompiled domain.
6. Existing `fleet-connect` has no secrets/crypto/PKI/generator dependency and remains ≤2 MiB stripped, with 1.5 MiB target.

## Negative tests and oracle
Negative: invocation alias requests capability absent from binary, connect invokes secrets/cert/generate, config enables uncompiled feature, command advertised available without implementation, and command aliases produce distinct semantics. Oracle: capability golden matrix, current CLI output fixtures, smoke invocations and Nix final-artifact size gate.

## Security and environment
Build/test only. No deployment, signing, provider access, secret mutation, trust/DNS change or new schedule. New commands remain unavailable stubs until their owner deliverables land.

## Dependencies, complexity, priority, lifecycle
Parent #9157; depends on ARCH-01/06 shared APIs and domain descriptors GEN-01/CERT-01 with soft coordination (not a blockedBy edge) with generated-help owner OPS-05. Complexity M; V2; proposed High / urgency 450; Backlog.

## Rollback and recovery
Revert only additive descriptors/feature edges; preserve current domain entries and variants. Verify `fleet-connect` and `get/list` fixtures after rollback. Do not remove a domain implementation owned by another proposal.

## Open decisions
Exact Nix artifact/profile packaging waits for measured dependency closure in ARCH-10. Capability naming/help additions wait for GEN-01/CERT-01/SEC domain schemas; avoid duplicate aliases.

## Priority semantics
The numeric `urgency` field is the shared charter intrinsic scale (lower is sooner); this score is High, distinct from importance, blocker, stage and dispatch. It is not the Project/queue priority. Do not change PM schema; any publisher maps High to queue priority 20 while retaining this numeric score and band in metadata/body.

title: Prove minimal profile dependency closure and ratify size/startup budgets
body:
## Why / user outcome
Give small Rust applications a measured runtime-only Fleet dependency closure while retaining a separate administrative build. Prevent optional secrets providers, PKI algorithms, CLI/admin features and publication dependencies from leaking into consumers or the existing connect artifact.

## Current repository evidence
The current `fleet` workspace has full/serve/connect Cargo feature sets and a 2 MiB hard cap/1.5 MiB target for stripped connect artifact (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/Cargo.toml`, `pkgs/fleet/default.nix`). No consumer-min or agent profile exists and no profile size/startup measurement was performed in the census.

## Scope and affected surface
Implement profile-to-feature mapping and build proof for: consumer-min (runtime resolver + explicitly selected minimal provider, no admin/PKI); agent (runtime read + receipts, no writer/admin by default); existing fleet; admin (explicit mutation/PKI/codecs); serve (broker role with selected providers). Affected files: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/Cargo.toml`, workspace `pkgs/fleet/Cargo.toml` only if needed for an optional shared crate, `pkgs/fleet/default.nix`, and profile/build tests under `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/tests/**`. Change only feature manifests, `default.nix`, and profile/build smoke tests. Domain crates remain owned by #9158/#9162/#9163/#9164. No runtime benchmark code for provider internals.

## Proposed budgets and measurable acceptance
1. Existing `fleet-connect` remains ≤2 MiB stripped hard max with 1.5 MiB target; it has no secrets/crypto/PKI links.
2. Provisional, unratified targets: consumer-min ≤3 MiB stripped with one selected provider; agent ≤8 MiB without PQ/OpenSSL; warm local startup p95 ≤25 ms; in-memory resolver overhead p95 ≤1 ms excluding provider I/O. These targets are not release gates until a baseline is measured and owner approves them.
3. Record exact compiler/toolchain, target, feature tree, binary bytes, startup method/sample count and p50/p95/p99 for each profile. Report any proposed target missed; do not call it passed by estimation.
4. Inspect dependency graph to prove provider/crypto/CLI feature isolation; a Rust symbol being unused is not proof it was not linked.
5. Nix reproducible build smoke passes for existing variants and proposed profiles.

## Negative tests and oracle
Negative: connect links `fleet-secrets`, crypto/PQ, PKI or admin; consumer-min compiles a write/admin method or unrelated serve/search stack; agent implicitly includes admin authority; profile name widens compiled capability; optional feature default unexpectedly enables dependency; size threshold reported without a measured artifact. Oracle: Cargo feature tree + linker/build artifact inspection + final Nix stripped file-size check + repeated process-start measurements with fixed environment.

## Security and environment
Local/CI builds and synthetic startup fixtures only. No live provider, secret, deploy, production config or schedule changes. Performance data records no credentials or secret values.

## Dependencies, complexity, priority, lifecycle
Parent #9157; depends on ARCH-07 feature descriptors and PERF-01 benchmark methodology. Complexity M; V2; proposed High / urgency 450; Backlog. Hard connect gate is existing contract; new budgets await baseline/approval.

## Rollback and recovery
Keep consumer/admin feature sets opt-in and additive. If dependency leakage or size regression appears, remove the new profile edge; existing full/serve/connect variants and interface remain unchanged. Retain measurements and build metadata for comparison.

## Open decisions
Ratify provisional size/startup targets only after baseline on reference laptop and CI target. Determine whether profiles become separate Nix outputs or only Cargo feature sets based on measured artifact/consumer need.

## Priority semantics
The numeric `urgency` field is the shared charter intrinsic scale (lower is sooner); this score is High, distinct from importance, blocker, stage and dispatch. It is not the Project/queue priority. Do not change PM schema; any publisher maps High to queue priority 20 while retaining this numeric score and band in metadata/body.

title: Implement the unified input-reference and output-target resolver with typed selectors
stage: V2 foundation; integrated by existing Fleet domain commands
body:
## Why / user outcome
Provide one typed library resolver for heterogeneous input references and one typed output-target plan consumed by existing Fleet commands. Users and embedded callers can select inputs/outputs without each domain inventing string guessing, format routing or private-output behavior. This is not a new CLI or a second secret resolver.

## Current repository evidence
At pinned census commit `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`, Fleet has a broker/BWS name resolver but no shared `InputRef`/`OutputTarget` module. ARCH-01 owns SecretRef/policy; ARCH-06 owns signer/output authorization; OPS-04 owns safe file/archive writes. Those are consumed, not reimplemented here.

## Scope and owned files/interfaces
Implement one cohesive reusable `fleet-io` crate because CLI, PKI, generation and embedded Rust have multiple real consumers of the same resolution/selection seam; do not create a crate per source or format. Proposed files: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-io/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs,tests/input_ref.rs,tests/output_target.rs}`, plus opt-in workspace/consumer feature wiring. It owns typed normalization and target planning only. It delegates secret reads to ARCH-01, authorization to ARCH-06, and physical file/archive transactions to OPS-04.

## API/CLI behavior
```rust
pub enum InputRef {
    File(PathBuf), DirectoryManifest(PathBuf), Archive(PathBuf), Stdin,
    Structured { format: InputFormat, bytes: Vec<u8> },
    PkiFingerprint(PublicFingerprint), LogicalId(CredentialId),
    SecretUri(QualifiedSecretUri), DefaultInventory(NonRootInventoryRef),
    ExplicitSignerHandle(ExplicitKeyRef), InMemory(MemoryArtifactRef),
}
pub enum OutputTarget {
    File(PathBuf), Directory(PathBuf), Archive(PathBuf),
    Stdout(PublicOutputMode), ProviderStore(ProviderId, ScopeId),
    Memory(SinkHandle), None,
}
pub async fn resolve_input(&self, request: InputRequest, cancel: CancellationToken)
    -> Result<ResolvedInput, InputError>;
pub async fn plan_output(&self, target: OutputTarget, artifact: ClassifiedArtifact,
                         cancel: CancellationToken) -> Result<OutputPlan, OutputError>;
```
`InputResolver` delegates SecretUri/LogicalId to ARCH-01; a signer-handle reference is a locator only and cannot create signing authority. DefaultInventory is permitted only for explicit non-root read purposes. OutputTarget is a plan, not a writer: confidential outputs require ARCH-06 `OutputAuthorization`; ProviderStore writes also require provider capability/operation grant, and file/archive commit goes through OPS-04. Example at an existing Fleet domain surface: `fleet cert bundle inspect --input <typed-ref> --dry-run --json`; no standalone executable or new command family is added by this packet.

Typed errors: `InvalidReference`, `AmbiguousInput { candidates: RedactedCandidate[] }`, `UnsupportedFormat`, `NotFound`, `ScopeDenied`, `PolicyDenied`, `UnsafeArchive`, `CapabilityUnavailable`, `Cancelled`, `Unavailable`. Ambiguous errors expose only redacted candidate refs, never values.

## Measurable acceptance
1. Normalize file, directory/manifest, archive, stdin, structured bytes, PKI fingerprint, stable ID, qualified secret URI, non-root inventory, explicit signer handle and in-memory artifact into typed variants.
2. Ambiguous matching sources fail with typed candidate diagnostics; no first-match, provider-speed or path/name guessing.
3. Secret resolution delegates to ARCH-01. Root default-inventory lookup and signer authority are denied; explicit signer handles do not act as grants.
4. OutputTarget covers file/directory/archive/stdout/provider-store/memory/none and public/private classification. Private bytes require exact plan/class/destination `OutputAuthorization`; public/stdout defaults exclude private material.
5. Archive parsing is bounded by total bytes, entry count and expansion; traversal, outside symlinks, duplicate normalized paths and bombs reject before extraction.
6. All candidate selection is explicit/deterministic; same label across input kinds is ambiguous unless a typed selector uniquely resolves it.
7. No filesystem/network/subprocess is required for an in-memory reference/plan; no dependency cycle with fleet-secrets, PKI or CLI.

## Negative tests and oracle
Property tests round-trip typed refs/aliases and ensure scopes never collide; a reference selector model determines exact unique/ambiguous outcomes. Fuzz archive parsing. Negative fixtures cover path/archive same basename, duplicate URI/ID candidate, root lookup through DefaultInventory, caller-supplied public classification, signer-handle-as-authority, private stdout without grant, unauthorized ProviderStore, path traversal, symlink escape, duplicate archive entries, excessive expansion and cancellation. Oracle: reference selector output, fixture hashes/entry set and zero provider/sink calls on denial.

## Security and safe environment
Synthetic inputs/targets only. No live providers, keys, stores, archive exports, file mutations, DNS/trust operations or credentials. RootPrivate stays out of ordinary resolution and caching. This is a V2 proposal; no V1 implementation is implied.

## Dependencies, priority, lifecycle, size, stage
Parent #9157; hard dependencies ARCH-01, ARCH-06 and OPS-04. Estimated size/complexity L; V2 foundation; Backlog; intrinsic urgency 600 (High), separate from importance/stage/queue projection.

## Failure, rollback, recovery
Resolution/planning is side-effect free until a separately authorized adapter operation. Invalid/ambiguous/unsafe input fails before read/write. Disable the optional fleet-io consumer edge to roll back; preserve V1 resolver and all existing commands.

Pin archive parser/limits after dependency/license/security review. Keep `fleet-io` one cohesive seam only if multiple consumers and dependency closure remain demonstrated; otherwise keep the module in the narrowest shared library. No per-format crate split.

title: Add the FleetContext composition facade and CLI/library parity harness
stage: V2 foundation; shared composition facade with domain-owned operations
body:
## Why / user outcome
Provide one embedded Rust composition facade so humans, scripts and Rust callers use the same typed operation semantics without invoking the Fleet binary internally. It composes domain-owned operations and injected ports; it does not become a domain-logic god object or a second authorization authority.

## Current repository evidence
At pinned census commit `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`, Fleet has a multicall binary and separate crates such as `fleet-secrets`, registry, config and queue, but no reusable `FleetContext` composition library. `fleet-secrets` is a name resolver, not a complete application context. ARCH-01/06/07/12 define runtime read, signer/artifact authority, CLI registry and input/output planning seams; domain proposals own PKI, generation, credential schema, reconciliation, sinks and receipts.

## Scope and owned files/interfaces
Add one reusable `fleet-context` facade crate because CLI and embedded Rust callers need the same cross-domain composition seam: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-context/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs,tests/parity.rs}`, workspace manifest and existing `fleet` binary adapter. Do not create per-domain wrappers/crates. The facade owns dependency construction, preflight and typed operation dispatch only; policy and operation logic remain in domain owners.

Proposed API:
```rust
pub struct FleetContextBuilder { /* ARCH-01 resolver/context, ARCH-12 input/output plans,
    ARCH-06 authorization/ledger/output ports, domain services, clock */ }
pub struct FleetContext { /* immutable composed ports */ }
impl FleetContext {
    pub async fn execute(&self, request: OperationRequest, cancel: CancellationToken)
        -> Result<OperationReceipt, ContextError>;
}
pub enum ContextError { MissingCapability, PolicyDenied, Unavailable, Partial,
                        Uncertain, Cancelled, Domain(DomainError) }
```
The builder receives authority ports/capabilities, not constructors for SigningAuthorization, DurableTupleClaim or OutputAuthorization. It may request authorization only after a domain has prepared exact bytes/tuple. CLI adapters parse/render only and call the same typed operation path. Root operations require explicit root-key identity/ceremony; no default signer exists.

## API/CLI example
```rust
let ctx = FleetContext::builder()
    .resolver(resolver).input_resolver(input_resolver)
    .signing_authorization(signing_port).tuple_ledger(ledger)
    .output_authorization(output_port).event_sink(events)
    .domain_services(fake_domains).build()?;
let receipt = ctx.execute(OperationRequest::SyntheticPipeline(plan), cancel).await?;
```
An existing Fleet domain command parses the equivalent versioned request and calls the same `execute`; this issue adds no standalone CLI. The library route never spawns Fleet. `fleet secrets get` keeps its separate legacy raw-value stdout behavior; typed structured receipts remain redacted.

## Measurable acceptance
1. One typed request through CLI adapter and embedded facade yields equivalent public result/error and redacted receipt under the same fake services.
2. An in-memory synthetic pipeline streams one fixture to two fake sinks (NATS→DB/Redis-shaped) with no process spawn, temp file or network.
3. Missing domain port returns typed MissingCapability before side effect; cancellation/partial/uncertain outcomes are preserved per operation and do not claim cross-sink atomicity.
4. Facade cannot construct or clone signer/output authority; root signing requires explicit key identity and the ARCH-06 final-tuple claim; private artifact output requires an exact output grant.
5. `fleet-connect` does not link the facade or its dependencies; minimal consumer dependency closure stays controlled by ARCH-10.

## Negative tests and oracle
MBT compares facade and CLI adapter states against a reference operation-result model. Negative cases: missing port, output mismatch, hidden subprocess, secret sentinel in structured receipt/log, duplicate effect after cancellation, root request without explicit key/ceremony/claim, private sink without destination grant, expired/wrong grant, and a facade operation bypassing domain policy. Oracle: canonical redacted request/receipt golden and fake invocation counters prove denied calls cause zero signer/sink actions.

## Security and safe environment
Synthetic values and fake services only. No live provider, production sign, secret write, NATS/DB/Redis service, deployment, schedule, DNS/trust change or root export. Builder carries explicitly injected authority ports but never mints authority.

## Dependencies, priority, lifecycle, size, stage
Parent #9157; hard dependencies ARCH-01, ARCH-06, ARCH-07 and ARCH-12. Estimated size/complexity L; V2 foundation; Backlog; intrinsic urgency 700 (High), separate from importance/stage/queue projection.

## Failure, rollback, recovery
Keep facade behind an optional feature and preserve existing direct domain APIs. On parity/authority regression disable the facade; no production state is changed. An uncertain operation is reconciled by its owning domain before retry.

## Open decisions
Validate that the facade crate has useful reuse and one-way dependency closure before extraction. Reversal trigger: if it starts owning domain policy or becomes a god object, move orchestration back to domain modules.
